object: rock graffito of eight lines, with a peculiar cruciform symbol on the right (the symbol is not printed)
site: Dakka: isolated table-shaped hill south of Gebel Abu Dirwa, three miles south-west of the temple (Lower Nubia), west face, clearly visible from below
notes: Rock graffito in archaic style, one of three found by O. Bates (Archaeological Survey of Nubia, Bulletin 5); Griffith's hand-copies of November 1910 and Firth's photographs (Pls. XI, XII). The letter in rem is Griffith's sub-number (91 a, b, c); REM's own form of the suffix was not checked. Griffith: the first word 'must be O Amanap', an invocation of the Theban Amenopi (otherwise only in the titles of his priests at Karanog); the rest is presumably largely proper names; the last word occurs in Meroe 6/1; the initial m is 7 cm high. In l. 5 Griffith prints a queried dot (lost sign) before p; written [.].
